lines: An AI-generated fix passed one hundred and fifty-five selected tests.
It still missed a second implementation. This is Patch Audit.
These are real saved results from Boltons, a Python utility library.
The ordinary suite passed. Open its execution log to inspect the retained output.
The task required both copies of the ordered multi-dictionary to handle one-shot iterables consistently.
That requirement was specified separately from the candidate patch.
The exact patch collects input once, then reuses it.
But the change affects only dictutils. The standalone copy in urlutils was left untouched.
Here is that untouched implementation. It consumes the iterable twice.
Normal package imports can hide the fallback used in standalone mode.
The independent empty-input check expected length zero. It observed length one, even though keys and items were empty.
These are observations of one incomplete repair.
Download the original evidence and exact patch.
Source, candidate, runtime and verifier identities bind the outcome to what actually ran.
Public visitors can inspect this saved evidence, but cannot execute patches.
The separate G3 study found zero additional independent issues across six historical developer patches.
To audit a new change, follow the local Docker quickstart.
Review immutable source, the patch and declared checks. Validate controls and approve the exact plans before execution.
